title: Remove a wire-mesh pulling grip from an installed cable
justification: Electrician cable installation uses temporary mesh grips; removal exploits axial compression of a self-tightening braid.
fault: Installed pulling sock remains tightened around cable after pull. This may be ordinary tool removal rather than a failure; do not invent a faulty latch.
instruction: Remove the temporary pulling grip and leave it beside the cable.
objects: Klein KPS050SEN165.1mm overall; compatible12.7–14.3mm unenergized cable with accessible end; source-based wire braid, swivel and clip. Other props/layout not chosen.
skill: Counterintuitive axial compression releases frictional braid contraction; preserve actual interwoven strands and cable contact.
scoring: Not finalized. Require separated released grip and intact cable using geometric observations; no unsupported continuity or permanent failed-pull penalty.
nearest: RoboARC fiber-bundling/knot tasks: compare physical topology and valid shortcuts before build
risks: Photo establishes form but not exact braid carrier count, wire diameter, mesh length or bending stiffness. Published safe load is not a local jacket-damage threshold.
Closed mesh requires accessible cable end. Do not add an oversized connector the real grip cannot pass; cable and termination geometry must match a real installation.

Simulation must retain over-under wire contacts and U-shaped mouth returns. Crossing welds, no-self-collision chains, shape-driven diameters or scripted grip-release flags would not establish physical fidelity.
Ordinary cablekit defaults are inappropriate:2mm contact offset and5e-6kgm2 armature exceed strand scales. Use round contacts, actual inertia, explicit convergence and torque/energy evidence.
A robot may compress the braid against the cable when pinching it. Need geometry/reach then physical release attempt at exact source scale.
Current board search braid/pulling grip/finger trap found no match; complete skill-level comparison still needed.
strict_review: Potentially distinct deformable contact skill with direct electrical-work relevance. Critical risk is a fake constrained-braid model or tiny inaccessible mouth; no submission or validation claim without physical component tests.
